nodes.content: Develop domain-generalization methods that distinguish transferable predictive features from spurious features without source-domain annotations or target-domain data.
requirements: Achieve ≥5 percentage points higher worst-domain accuracy than ERM under unseen combinations of spurious correlations.
Keep average source-domain accuracy within one percentage point of ERM while preserving genuinely predictive features.

nodes.content: Train SwapAnchor by exchanging inferred nuisance codes across labels, enforcing counterfactual consistency, and distilling ERM on original examples.
How can SwapAnchor infer exchangeable nuisance codes without stripping predictive structure when spurious cues co-occur with genuine features?
Within-class residual clustering after supervised bottlenecking isolates exchangeable nuisance codes; ERM distillation limits source-accuracy loss to ≤1 point.
Fit a supervised bottleneck, cluster within-class residuals, swap codes across labels, then audit causal-feature retention and source accuracy on ColorShape-Mix.
Train SwapAnchor using four within-class residual clusters, cross-label nuisance swaps, and ERM distillation; score source and unseen ColorShape-Mix combinations.
ColorShape-Mix v1 report contains SwapAnchor and ERM checkpoints, inferred nuisance-cluster assignments, causal-feature probes, and source/unseen accuracy tables.
Using ColorShape-Mix v1 checkpoints, ablate residual clustering and distillation; measure nuisance-code purity, causal-probe retention, and source-accuracy gap versus ERM.
On ColorShape-Mix v1, distilled SwapAnchor lost 2.8 source-accuracy points versus ERM; without distillation, it lost 5.1.
Using ColorShape-Mix v1 checkpoints, swap individual residual clusters across labels to identify shape-information leakage and causal-probe failures.
Two residual clusters had 91% color purity and ≤0.5-point shape-probe loss under swaps; the others leaked shape.
Can source-only intervention tests identify safe residual clusters without shape labels and reduce SwapAnchor’s 2.8-point source-accuracy deficit?
GateSwap filters residual swaps by self-supervised instance-neighbor stability, retaining ERM distillation and targeting ≤1-point source-accuracy loss versus ERM.
Rank residual clusters by source-only instance-neighbor stability under swaps; gate interventions, then compare GateSwap source accuracy against SwapAnchor and ERM.
Sweep source-only GateSwap stability thresholds; compare selected clusters with ColorShape-Mix leakage audit and source-accuracy loss with SwapAnchor’s 2.8-point deficit.
On ColorShape-Mix v1, GateSwap’s 0.9 stability gate isolated color-pure clusters, reducing source-accuracy loss from 2.8 to 0.7 points.
Advance GateSwap’s 0.9 stability gate to unseen-correlation testing because it selected color-pure clusters with only 0.7-point source-accuracy loss.
CrossRisk clusters class-conditional residual gradients into pseudo-domains, optimizes worst-cluster risk, and anchors source predictions to ERM.
Do residual-gradient pseudo-domains capture distinct spurious-correlation combinations, or merely partition examples by difficulty?
Residual-gradient clusters will recover evaluation-only color–background combinations (AMI ≥0.30), outperforming loss-matched difficulty bins (AMI ≤0.10) on ColorShape-Mix v1.
Fit class-conditional residual-gradient clusters and loss-matched difficulty bins on ColorShape-Mix v1; compare evaluation-only color–background AMI.
On ColorShape-Mix v1, residual-gradient clusters achieved color–background AMI 0.08, nearly matching difficulty bins at 0.06.
Audit gradient-cluster loss distributions, residualize gradients against difficulty, then compare color–background AMI with loss-matched bins.
Given 0.08 AMI baseline, regress gradient vectors on per-example loss, recluster residuals, and recompute color–background AMI against difficulty bins.
Original clusters’ class-conditional AMI was 0.34 versus difficulty bins’ 0.07, resolving n18’s pooled-label artifact; loss-residualized clusters scored 0.36.
Does worst-cluster training on loss-residualized pseudo-domains improve unseen-combination accuracy without erasing shape features or exceeding one-point source loss?
CrossRisk-Guard minimizes worst loss-residualized cluster risk subject to ≤1-point ERM source-accuracy loss and ≥95% instance-neighbor retention.
Train CrossRisk-Guard with source-only constraints, then report unseen-combination worst-domain accuracy, source gap, and shape-probe retention versus ERM.
Given pooled AMI 0.08 and residualized class-conditional AMI 0.36, train CrossRisk-Guard; measure unseen worst-domain accuracy, source gap, shape retention.
On ColorShape-Mix v1, CrossRisk-Guard raised unseen worst-domain accuracy 61.8%→68.1%, with 0.8-point source loss, 96% neighbor and 97% shape-probe retention.
Does CrossRisk-Guard’s worst-cluster objective overfit pseudo-domains containing fewer than 5% of source examples?
Excluding pseudo-domains below 5% source prevalence improves unseen worst-domain accuracy by ≥2 points without exceeding one-point source loss.
Sweep CrossRisk-Guard pseudo-domain minimum prevalence from 0% to 10%; compare unseen worst-domain accuracy and source gap across seeds.
Against CrossRisk-Guard’s 68.1% baseline, sweep 0%, 2%, 5%, 10% prevalence floors over five seeds; assess worst-domain accuracy and source loss.
Five-seed reruns: 5% floor raised worst-domain accuracy 68.1%→70.4%, with 0.9-point source loss; baseline CrossRisk-Guard lost 1.3 points.
Pair seeds across baseline and 5%-floor reruns, reconciling 0.8/1.3-point source gaps and testing ≥2-point worst-domain gains and ≤1-point source loss.
Seed-paired analysis found only a 1.4-point worst-domain gain, versus 2.3 unpaired; the 5% floor retained 0.9-point source loss.
Which rare pseudo-domains carry transferable shape cues that a fixed prevalence floor would discard?
Sub-5% clusters with ≥95% neighbor stability preserve shape cues; reliability-weighted risk improves worst-domain accuracy ≥2 points over 5% filtering.
Audit sub-5% clusters with shape probes; weight risks using source-only neighbor stability, then compare paired-seed accuracy against 5% filtering.
Audit sub-5% clusters’ shape-probe retention; compare stability-weighted risk, 5%-floor, and CrossRisk-Guard across paired seeds on worst-domain accuracy and source loss.
On ColorShape-Mix v2, paired 5%-floor gained 2.2 worst-domain points versus unfiltered at 0.9-point source loss; stability-weighting trailed filtering.
Reconcile v1 unpaired/paired and v2 paired results by probing sub-5% cluster stability, shape retention, and weighted-versus-filtered worst-domain accuracy.
On v1, ≥95%-stable sub-5% clusters retained 98% shape-probe accuracy; stability-weighted risk beat 5%-floor by 2.1 worst-domain points, unlike v2.
Why does stability-weighted risk outperform 5% filtering on ColorShape-Mix v1 but trail it on v2?
Compare v1/v2 sub-5% cluster composition, neighbor stability, shape-probe retention, and per-cluster contributions to worst-domain errors.
Ablate ≥95%-stable sub-5% clusters separately on v1/v2, comparing shape-probe retention and worst-domain errors against 5%-floor baselines.
v1/v2 cluster-ablation ledger records sub-5% prevalence, neighbor stability, shape-probe retention, and worst-domain error changes versus 5%-floor baselines.
